name: Boat shoes

lead: Boat shoes are low leather or canvas shoes with a moccasin-style toe, hand-stitched look and grooved non-marking rubber soles. They were designed for grip on wet boat decks and became everyday casual footwear.
For looks, they add a nautical, preppy touch to shorts, chinos or linen in warm weather, and are traditionally worn without socks.

paras: People pair them with chinos, shorts or lightweight summer trousers and casual shirts. Leather versions suit smart-casual outfits, and canvas versions suit beachwear. Leather is typically oil-treated for water resistance.
Footwear carries no medical risk beyond fit; the sockless style can leave feet damp in heat. Style associations (preppy, coastal) may not match every dress code.

angle.text: Boat shoes dress down a smart-casual outfit with a classic, recognizable shape. Worn with shorts or chinos, they add a coastal, preppy touch.

lead: Boat shoes, also called deck shoes or top-siders, are casual shoes in canvas or leather with a moccasin-style toe, durable stitching and non-marking rubber soles cut with grooves for grip on wet decks.[1]

Paul A. Sperry of New Haven, Connecticut, is credited with inventing the modern boat shoe in 1935 after noticing his dog ran on ice without slipping and cutting grooves into a sole; this led to the Sperry Top-Sider brand.[1]
People wear them for a relaxed nautical or preppy look. They have been everyday casual footwear in many coastal areas since the 1970s, trended in the 1980s and returned in the late 2000s.[1]

paras: The shoe typically has oil-treated leather or canvas, moccasin construction, durable stitching and a grooved, non-marking sole intended for wet surfaces.[1] They are traditionally worn without socks.[1]

Sperry introduced the modern design in 1935.[1] Sailors wore them first; from the 1970s they spread as casual wear, trending in the 1980s and again in the late 2000s.[1] Their association with boat ownership gave them some status, and they appear in nautical and preppy fashion.[1] Some schools allow them because they are leather.[1]

timeline.event: Paul Sperry invents the modern boat shoe.[1]

Trend peak; Sebago, Sperry and Eastland among the popular brands.[1]
